independent_solutions.solver_a:
Step 1: System definition: Consider the disc and the insect as a combined mechanical system rotating about the fixed vertical axis through the center of the disc.
Step 2: External torque: There are no external horizontal torques acting on the system about the vertical axis of rotation (assuming frictionless axle/bearing), so the net external torque about the vertical axis is zero: tau_{ext, z} = 0.
Step 3: Conservation of angular momentum: The total angular momentum of the system about the vertical axis is conserved: L_z = I_{total}(r) * omega(r) = constant.
independent_solutions.solver_b:
Step 1: Identify the physical system comprising the thin horizontal circular disc of mass M and radius R and an insect of mass m moving along a diameter.
Step 2: Check for external torques about the vertical axis passing through the centre of the disc. Assuming ideal frictionless bearings, there is no net external torque about the rotation axis (tau_ext = 0). The frictional and contact forces between the insect and disc are internal to the system.
Step 3: By the principle of conservation of angular momentum about the fixed vertical axis of rotation: L_z = I_total(r) * omega(r) = constant.
